text:
tariq: FYI saw a microburst on pool-C around 02:14 that triggered host OOM kills. Not same as the large-page evict cases; looks like tiny allocations piling up in freelists and not coalescing fast enough.

julie: ouch. which allocator? tiny-slab or shadow-buddy?

tariq: tiny-slab. pattern: many tenants create ~64B scratch buffers for tokenization then free them immediately. freelist metadata keeps them as fragmented subslots. Over 3m we accumulated ~600k fragments across 12 hosts.

ben: can you paste memstat snapshot?

tariq: memstat: 
```
slab:small slots_total=65536 slots_used=23418 util=35% fragments=612345
slab:medium slots_total=32768 slots_used=12000 util=36% fragments=0
host_rss=7.8GB -> 10.1GB over 3m
```
fragments are almost exclusively 64/128B.

noah: is this a recluster timing issue or freelist merge bug?

tariq: both. recluster runs infrequently and our coalescer is conservative: it only merges when two adjacent free slots are both cold and the slab writeback quiescent bit is clear. Under heavy churn the quiescent bit never clears.

julie: proposal: introduce freelist aging with epoch counters. When a slot is freed increment epoch. If free_epoch - slab_epoch > K, treat as stale and allow coalesce even if recently-touched. Also add a probabilistic opportunistic-merge on alloc path with a tiny CPU budget.

ben: probabilistic merges on alloc path worry me because allocs are hot on p99. But if we do it with a cheap 1-in-1024 coin flip and limit work to one merge per flip it might be okay. Need safe fast path.

noah: another idea: per-tenant recycled pool. If tenant scrubs frequently, keep a small tenant-local cache of 64B objects so we avoid polluting slab-wide free lists. Eviction of tenant cache happens LRU.

julie: that helps multi-tenant isolation but increases bookkeeping. Also some tenants already use ephemeral scratch heavily so their local cache could grow. Need caps.

ben: tradeoffs: freelist-aging reduces long tail memory in shared slabs, tenant-cache reduces cross-tenant fragmentation but adds per-tenant memory. Which is more desirable?

sophie: ops perspective: prefer a default that reduces host RSS spikes without tenant opt-ins. So freelist-aging as default + tenant-cache opt-in for premium pools sounds reasonable.

julie: ok design sketch: 
- add slab_epoch (u32) bump every recluster cycle
- free_slot sets slot_free_epoch = current_epoch and pushes to freelist
- coalescer: if (slot_free_epoch + AGE_THRESH < current_epoch) allow forced merge ignoring recent-touch
- opportunistic_alloc_flip: on allocation, 1/1024 chance to try one adjacent-merge to reduce fragmentation; measure CPU cost.
- tenant_cache: per-pool ring buffer up to N entries, LRU on miss. configurable.

noah: locking model? coalescer must hold slab lock; opportunistic_alloc should try CAS to steal neighbor and if fails continue allocation. Avoid long holds.

ben: telemetry: counters freelist_forced_merges, opportunistic_alloc_triggers, tenant_cache_hits, tenant_cache_evictions, slab_epoch_advances. Also histograms for merge_latency and alloc_p99_before/after.

julie: rollout: feature-flagged, enable forced-merge on 5% nodes for 12h, measure host_rss_delta and p99_alloc_latency. If good, expand to 50% then all. tenant_cache disabled by default.

sophie: automation: ops-bot should kill the feature flag automatically if host_rss increases >200MB or alloc_p99 regresses >10ms for >5m.

ops-bot: monitor/flag created: freelist-aging-canary for pool-C. Auto rollback thresholds set.

tariq: micro-bench prototype showed 42% drop in fragment count on test harness with ~1% CPU overhead and no measurable alloc p99 regression. I'll attach logs to RFC.

noah: follow-up: need to formalize invariants for slot epoch wraparound. Use saturating arithmetic to avoid stale comparisons. Also ensure epoch increments are cheap.

julie: I'll author RFC with pseudocode + microbench results and a simple correctness proof sketch about merges not losing live objects. Can someone add tenant_cache config knobs?

ben: I will. Also we should add a safe-mode: if kernel OOM killer was active recently, raise AGE_THRESH to force faster merges.

sophie: agree. that helps emergency recovery.

tariq: thanks team. RFC requested; will ping when draft link is up. We should also include small bash snippets to reproduce the churn pattern.

julie: nice. ping me for review. :thumbsup:
